note: AUTHORED living-layer boundaries (water and foliage) in MASTER px. These exist because the material mask fails above the river: mask-bare-ground looks for bright low-variance silk and the dry CLIFF up here is bright low-variance silk too — living/native/w-midstream/mask-overlay.png is blue confetti over rock, and 449 mask components with a largest of 6487px is what that looks like numerically. What separates water here is pictorial, so it is authored by eye against gridded master crops (living/grid-crop.py), the same loop the 31 stations used. Two inventory boxes in regions.json were also refuted by looking: f-left-tall-fall [980,8650,1330,10100] is bare cliff and canopy — the real gorge fall is a slender white column at x~1470-1610 running y 9040-10620; and w-upper-stream is not a stream at all, it is the same fall's lower half.
